methodology.date: Exact visit date remains null unless verified. An assigned year is approximate, and a range is retained as a range.

methodology.musicAndDining: Attending a restaurant with live jazz does not automatically count as a distinct concert. Require a separately confirmed performance before adding a concert record.
methodology.awardFocusedCollection: Default Culture Passport Dining chapter shows only venues with verified historical Michelin inclusion or James Beard recognition of restaurant itself or chef at that restaurant. Memory-only confirmed visits are preserved but hidden by default, discoverable with a separate toggle. Recognition year may differ from dinner year.
methodology.curated: Default Culture Passport dining views show confirmed restaurants with documented Michelin Guide recognition (star, Bib, Selected, historic Plate) or directly associated James Beard awards, finalists or semifinalists. Those awards retain their recipient and year. Chef awards at unrelated restaurants or historical awards dated after a dinner may be context, not proof of qualification at the meal date. Unverified and outside-scope visits stay in archive but are hidden from curated browsing by default.
methodology.featuredExceptions: Venue-specific Michelin/JBF honors are the default inclusion criteria, but the user's express favorites Sauvage, Gunther & Co., Death & Co Denver and provisional favorite The Majestic are displayed in the primary collection despite no established qualifying award. FiNO was added as a user-selected confirmed 2026 visit without award recognition; this does not imply it is a personal favorite.
methodology.beverages: Stand-alone cocktail bars are type=bar, never counted as restaurants. James Beard Outstanding Bar Program includes bar semifinalists. Never borrow recognition from another location within a chain.
methodology.repeatVisits: A venue may be visited in multiple years. Each confirmed year is represented as a separate experience record with a stable unique ID, sharing one venue ID; do not manufacture precise calendar dates or collapse years into one event.
methodology.reservationEvidence: Date and party size from completed reservation screenshots are documentary evidence, not independent proof of check-in or dining. Only directly restaurant-level Michelin/JBF recognition enters the curated collection automatically. The user explicitly excluded Le Fou Frog: it must not enter any deployed venue/experience ledger, even though its date appears in private conversation uploads.
methodology.storyFirst: Each published entry leads with a grounded personal memory, atmosphere, or occasion. Dates are retained in provenance but the public timeline emphasizes approximate years, seasons, and meaningful events. Never fabricate meals, companion details, specific actions, or feelings not supplied by the user.
methodology.dateDisplay: Date/party details are backend evidence, available in a collapsed archive-notes section on experience pages, not default cards or timeline. Exact date may be shown only if necessary to a user-given occasion (Valentine's Day, etc.).
methodology.familyStory: A venue may carry a narrative across sister restaurants or expansions. Guide badges identify the recognized original without treating each branch as a separate unverified award.
methodology.criterionAudit: Keep separate: verified Michelin Guide inclusion (stars, Bib, Selected/historical Plate), James Beard semifinalist/finalist/winner at the specific venue or chef while working there, explicitly featured personal memories, user-confirmed history without award, uncertain leads, and reservation-only evidence. Never count unverified founders' awards from unrelated restaurants or award years as the historical dining year.
methodology.stageMemories: Confirmed live outings can be recorded with a provisional production title. Verify the tour period and venue independently but do not infer exact performance dates; labels are about the memory.
methodology.culturalExperiences: Concert, festival, theatrical, live television, magic and opera entries can be supported by user recollections or personal event archive screenshots without Michelin/James Beard recognition. Show exact performance dates only when supported; a run's date window never proves a particular night.
methodology.reservationDisambiguation: Confirmed venue attendance never makes a completed reservation date a confirmed meal date. story.headline: Steaks and jazz inside a century of Kansas City history
paragraphs: Before the name came back, you remembered the combination: a wonderful Kansas City steakhouse with a jazz room down in the basement. That distinctive atmosphere brought you back to The Majestic. The year of your dinner remains open; the place itself is confirmed.

The building at 931 Broadway was originally Fitzpatrick's Saloon, opened in 1911. Its cellar took on a different life during Prohibition, when the lower level was used as a speakeasy. That room is today's Jazz Club—a link between the city's storied nightlife and the steakhouse you remembered.

The historic building was restored in the 1980s, and the Majestic name returned to the site in the early 1990s. The current restaurant opened under that name in November 2009, bringing dry-aged Kansas City steaks and live jazz together. It is an experience worth keeping for its atmosphere, regardless of Michelin or James Beard status.

story.headline: A basement cocktail room that helped change Kansas City
paragraphs: You remembered Manifesto as an amazing cocktail-bar experience. What stands out is its hidden, subterranean character—a room defined by candlelight, old stone walls, and carefully made drinks. The exact night is unknown, and there's no need to invent one.

Bartender Ryan Maybee opened Manifesto in 2009 beneath the building at 1924 Main Street. The intimate speakeasy paired a deliberately old-school atmosphere with a modern approach to classic cocktails. A temporary interruption followed the closure of the upstairs restaurant in 2010; the bar later returned alongside the Rieger Hotel Grill & Exchange.

Manifesto became an influential part of Kansas City's craft-cocktail identity. Its history also connects to the revival of J. Rieger & Co., a local distilling name that Maybee helped bring back. For this Passport, though, the reason for inclusion starts with your own memory of the place.

records.summary: An autumn dinner at North Pond, hidden inside Chicago's Lincoln Park, in the week following the 2021 Chicago Marathon. The restaurant occupies a century-old ice-skating warming house on the edge of a pond and held one Michelin star during the visit. A peaceful, seasonal counterpoint to the energy of marathon week.

story.headline: A quiet table in Lincoln Park, after marathon week
paragraphs: The memorable part begins before reaching the table. North Pond sits not on a busy downtown restaurant row, but tucked into the trees beside a pond in Lincoln Park. Its low Arts and Crafts-style building was constructed in 1912 as a warming shelter for ice skaters; decades later, that same refuge became a place for thoughtful, seasonal American cooking.

The restaurant's reputation was built in no small part by chef Bruce Sherman, whose focus on Midwestern ingredients earned him the James Beard Foundation's Best Chef: Great Lakes award in 2012. Sherman stepped away from daily kitchen leadership at the end of 2019, but the restaurant's identity endured.

In October 2021, during the week after the Chicago Marathon, this was one of the restaurants worth seeking out. That year's Michelin Guide had awarded North Pond one star months before the meal. The precise evening and dishes are not recorded; what survives is the setting, the post-race trip to Chicago, and a restaurant whose story reaches back more than a century.
